To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the International Transport Workers Federation (ITF) uses a combination of local and global strategies to organize workers in the transport sector.

the International Transport Workers Federation (ITF), the global union federation of transport workers, has been able to organize in transnational companies by focusing on single sites, which we have termed ‘resonant’ places.
the International Transport Workers Federation has developed an organizing strategy that focuses on single-site campaigns in order to create ‘resonant spaces’ for global union power.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: how do workers in a transnational union organize in the context of transnational corporations?
how to make the most of the power of the local in a globalizing world.
the question of how to organize across space, rather than how to organize in space.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the union’s organizing programme should continue to focus on single sites, while simultaneously building the capacity of workers to connect across different sites.

single site organizing is a key component of a broader global organizing strategy, and that the concept of a resonant place is a useful tool for understanding the role of such campaigns in a global organizing strategy.
the ITF has developed a strategy of organizing that has been effective in the short-term, but which has not yet delivered the long-term structural changes that the organization has sought.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ITF is working towards the creation of resonant places.
this research project has provided a new perspective for the analysis of labour organizing in transnational firms.

the International Transport Workers Federation is an organization that has a long and proud history of organizing in the transport sector and is now working to develop its organizing strategy in line with the challenges of global supply chains.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the International Trade Union Confederation and its affiliated organizations should be thinking about how to develop a global union strategy that builds on these single-site campaigns, rather than seeking to replace them with a more abstract and distant form of transnational organizing.
single site struggles can be powerful, but they must be connected to wider organizing efforts.
the power of unions lies in the power of their workers.
